name: University of California, Berkeley
meets_full_need_notes: UC Berkeley, as a public university, does not guarantee to meet 100% of demonstrated financial need. Average need met is approximately 83% for domestic students. California residents receive significantly better aid via Cal Grant and Blue and Gold Opportunity Plan.
no_loan_notes: UC Berkeley does not have a no-loan policy. Loans are standard components of most aid packages. The Blue and Gold Opportunity Plan covers fees/tuition for California residents with family incomes under $80,000, but does not eliminate loans from packages entirely.

merit_thresholds.notes: UC Berkeley offers Regents' and Chancellor's Scholarships (highly competitive, renewable). Most merit aid comes from departmental and external scholarships rather than central institutional grants.

ed_aid_implications: UC Berkeley does not offer ED or EA. All applicants are reviewed in the regular decision pool.
special_programs: UC Blue and Gold Opportunity Plan (tuition/fees covered for CA residents under $80k income)
appeal_policy: UC Berkeley students may appeal their financial aid package through the Financial Aid and Scholarships Office by submitting a Special Circumstances Appeal form. Appeals are considered for significant changes in family finances, unusual medical expenses, or data errors.
